title: Valproate hyperammonemic encephalopathy
consultQuestion: Patient on valproate with new lethargy, vomiting, confusion, or hypothermia — hyperammonemic encephalopathy?
keyHistory: Valproate start or dose change — hyperammonemic encephalopathy after starting valproate is reported in urea cycle disorders (label §5.6)
UCD risk features: unexplained encephalopathy/coma, encephalopathy after a protein load, pregnancy-related or postpartum encephalopathy, cyclical vomiting and lethargy, family history (label §5.6)
Concomitant topiramate — hyperammonemia ± encephalopathy even when each drug alone was tolerated (label §5.9)
Intentional or accidental overdose; amount ingested (Perrott)
keyExam: Lethargy, vomiting, change in mental status (label §5.8)
Core temperature — hypothermia <35 °C with or without hyperammonemia (label §5.10)
redFlags: Acute ingestion >100 mg/kg or valproate level >850 mg/L — higher risk of coma, respiratory depression, aspiration (Perrott)
Abdominal pain with vomiting — pancreatitis (boxed warning)

clues: Raised ammonia; can occur with normal liver tests (label §5.8)

differential.dx: Urea cycle disorder unmasked by valproate
clues: Encephalopathy after starting valproate; risk features in label §5.6
Somnolence, heart block, deep coma, hypernatremia (label §10); peak level can be delayed (Perrott)

notes: Any unexplained lethargy, vomiting, mental-status change, or hypothermia on valproate (label §5.8, §5.10)
Normal LFTs do not exclude hyperammonemia (label §5.8)
Overdose: peak at mean 7.4 h, ~15% >10 h after ingestion — repeat levels (Perrott)

decisionRules.condition: On valproate with unexplained lethargy, vomiting, mental-status change, or hypothermia

decisionRules.recommendation: Stop valproate; treat hyperammonemia; evaluate for urea cycle disorder
Monitor ammonia closely; consider stopping valproate if it persists

decisionRules.condition: Acute valproate overdose (>100 mg/kg) with decreased level of consciousness
decisionRules.recommendation: Consider IV L-carnitine 100 mg/kg, then 50 mg/kg (max 3 g/dose) IV q8h until ammonia is falling (if raised) and the patient improves
evidenceNote: Perrott 2010: authors' regimen from 8 case reports; no comparative data
Not a source for VHE on therapeutic dosing — chronic-therapy toxicity was excluded from the review

decisionRules.recommendation: Hemodialysis (± hemoperfusion) can remove significant drug; naloxone may reverse CNS depression — use with caution in epilepsy

initialSteps: Stop valproate if ammonia is raised (label §5.8); choose an alternative ASM — see antiseizure-medications
institutionVaries: Ammonia specimen handling (e.g., on ice, prompt analysis) — follow lab instructions
pearls: Hyperammonemia can occur with normal LFTs (label §5.8)
Topiramate + valproate hyperammonemia is not a pharmacokinetic interaction (label §5.9)
In overdose, ammonia didn't correlate with symptoms or outcome — don't use it alone to decide on L-carnitine (Perrott)
Hypothermia may be the presenting sign (label §5.10)
sources: Valproate sodium injection US prescribing information. Hikma; revised 12/2023 (user-supplied label)
Perrott J, Murphy NG, Zed PJ. L-Carnitine for Acute Valproic Acid Overdose: A Systematic Review of Published Cases. Ann Pharmacother 2010;44:1287-1293
